items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: The first time I played with three trumpets was when Gus Mo Clung... came back in the orchestra. So Gus joined our band in Cincinnati

ctx.x: Cincinnati when Joe Smith was on the stand sitting in with the local band, but now I was not afraid to play at the same dance as he and someone told me that Don Redman asked who I was because he liked the way I played.

The first time I played with three trumpets was when Gus Mo Clung, whom I had first heard with Scott, came back in the orchestra. Gus had a dispute with Don Redman when Scott had been in New York long before I joined them. Gus played with Clarence Page in Cincinnati in preparation to joining the Cotton Pickers after he left Scott and when Don was engaged to lead the Cotton Pickers, the first thing he did was to fire Gus.

So Gus joined our band in Cincinnati and Lloyd let Frank Newton go when we returned to the Savoy. We were in the Savoy when Marion Hardy's Alabamians came with Cab Calloway who sang through a megaphone three feet long. Eddie Mallory, one of the trumpet players became one of the ex-husbands and Charlie 'Fat Man' Turner eventually opened a bar called 'Fat Man's' on 155th Street and St. Nicholas Avenue that became very popular.
